## 1. Motivation:

```{r}
#| label: rainfall-ferns
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 5.7
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-alt: "Daily rainfall at Ferns III during May 2024."

library(ggplot2)

rain <- read.csv(
  "data/dly4715_subset.csv",
  skip = 9,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

may <- rain[
  grepl("-may-2024$", tolower(rain$date)) &
    !is.na(rain$rain),
]

may$date <- as.Date(
  sub("-may-", "-05-", tolower(may$date)),
  format = "%d-%m-%Y"
)

peak <- may[which.max(may$rain), , drop = FALSE]

may$highlight <- ifelse(
  may$date == peak$date,
  "Peak rainfall",
  "Daily rainfall"
)

x_days <- seq(1, 29, by = 4)

ggplot(may, aes(x = date, y = rain)) +
  geom_col(
    aes(fill = highlight),
    width = 0.78
  ) +
  geom_label(
    data = peak,
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f mm", rain)),
    vjust = -0.45,
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#9F3638",
    fill = "white",
    linewidth = 0,
    label.padding = grid::unit(0.18, "lines")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Daily rainfall" = "#4E86B4",
      "Peak rainfall" = "#CF5B5D"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = as.Date(
      sprintf("2024-05-%02d", x_days)
    ),
    labels = sprintf("%02d May", x_days),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 30, 10),
    limits = c(0, 35),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    subtitle = "Daily precipitation at Ferns III · May 2024",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Rainfall (mm)"
  ) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 21,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#27313A",
      margin = margin(b = 18)
    ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 17,
      color = "#38434C",
      margin = margin(r = 12)
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      angle = 35,
      hjust = 1,
      color = "#53606A"
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14,
      color = "#53606A"
    ),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "#E3E8EC",
      linewidth = 0.7
    ),
    plot.background = element_rect(
      fill = "transparent",
      color = NA
    ),
    panel.background = element_rect(
      fill = "transparent",
      color = NA
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 20, 8, 10)
  )
```

## 1.2 What is a Pulse event? {.smaller}

Definition: “Pulse Events [are] defined as abrupt changes in ecological parameters, are often present in ecosystems and include a wide array of phenomena, such as heat waves, marine upwelling, mass reproductive and mortality events, and biomass‐altering disturbances”

<div style="font-size: 16px; color: #68737d; margin-top: -15px;">
Jentsch and White (2019), Yang et al. (2008)
</div>

## 2. Methods: PPSI framework


$$
{\mathrm{PPSI}}=
\sqrt[3]{
\color{#006837}{S}
\cdot
\color{#72368d}{M}
\cdot
\color{#45bcbb}{C}
}
$$

<p style="text-align: center; color: #617086; font-size: 22px; margin-top: -5px; margin-bottom: 25px;">
Equal-weighted geometric mean of three normalized components
</p>

::: {.r-hstack style="justify-content: space-between; align-items: flex-start; text-align: center; gap: 35px;"}

::: {style="width: 30%;"}
<span style="color: #006837; font-size: 52px; font-weight: 700;">S</span>

**Source presence**

<span style="color: #617086; font-size: 21px;">
Where are agricultural sources present?
</span>
:::

::: {style="width: 30%;"}
<span style="color: #72368d; font-size: 52px; font-weight: 700;">M</span>

**Mobilization potential**

<span style="color: #617086; font-size: 21px;">
Can rainfall mobilize the material?
</span>
:::

::: {style="width: 30%;"}
<span style="color: #45bcbb; font-size: 52px; font-weight: 700;">C</span>

**Hydrological connectivity**

<span style="color: #617086; font-size: 21px;">
Can it reach the stream network?
</span>
:::

:::

## 2.2 PPSI Building

::: {.r-stack}
$$
\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{S} \cdot M \cdot C}
$$

::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index="1"}
$$
\mathrm{PPSI} =
\sqrt[3]{\color{#e12300}{\mathbf{S}} \cdot M \cdot C}
$$
:::

:::

- <span class="fragment highlight-red" data-fragment-index="1">**S: Source Presence**</span>

- **M**: Mobilization potential

- **C**: Hydrological connectivity

## 2.2.1 Agricultural Source Presence [S] {transition="fade" transition-speed="slow"}

::: {.r-stretch .r-vstack}
$$
S = \max(\mathit{cropland\_fraction},\mathit{grassland\_fraction})
$$
:::
::: {.footer}
$\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{\color{#e12300}{\mathbf{S}} \cdot M \cdot C}$
:::

## 2.2 PPSI Building

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index="1"}
$$
\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{S} \cdot M \cdot C}

- **S**: Source Presence
- <span class="fragment highlight-red" data-fragment-index="1">**M: Mobilization potential**</span>
- **C**: Hydrological connectivity

## 2.2.2 Mobilization [M] {transition="fade" transition-speed="slow"}

::: {.r-vstack style="width: 100%; gap: 0;"}
$$M = R^{0.60} \cdot B^{0.40}$$

::: {.fragment .fade-in data-fragment-index="1" style="width: 100%;"}
$$\swarrow \hspace{12em} \searrow$$

::: {.r-hstack style="width: 100%; justify-content: space-between; margin-top: -15px;"}
::: {data-id="rainfall-formula" style="width: 42%; text-align: center;" .fragment .highlight-red}
$$R = \sqrt{\mathit{Intensity} \cdot \mathit{Frequency}}$$
<div style="font-size: 18px; color: #617086;">Rainfall pulse</div>
:::
::: {data-id="soil-formula" style="width: 42%; text-align: center;"}
$$B = f(\mathit{soil\ texture\ classes})$$
<div style="font-size: 18px; color: #617086;">Soil runoff derived from texture class</div>
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.footer}
$\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{S} \cdot \color{#e12300}{\mathbf{M}} \cdot C}$
:::

## 2.2 PPSI Building

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index="1"}
$$
\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{S} \cdot M \cdot C}
$$
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index="1"}
$$
\mathrm{PPSI} = \sqrt[3]{{\mathbf{S}} \cdot M \cdot \color{#e12300}C}
$$
:::
:::

- **S**: Source Presence
- **M**: Mobilization potential
-  <span class="fragment highlight-red" data-fragment-index="1">**C: Hydrological connectivity**</span>

## 2.2.3 Hydrological Connectivity [C] {transition="fade" transition-speed="slow"}

::: {.r-stretch .r-vstack}

$$
C =
0.15F_{\mathrm{slope}}
+ 0.45F_{\mathrm{stream}}
+ 0.40F_{\mathrm{HAND}}
$$

<div style="font-size: 18px; color: #617086; margin-top: 15px;">
Weighted combination of normalized connectivity factors
</div>

:::

::: {.footer}
$\mathrm{PPSI} =
\sqrt[3]{\mathbf{S} \cdot M \cdot
\color{#e12300}{\mathbf{C}}}$
:::


## 2.2.3 Connectivity components {transition="fade" transition-speed="slow"}

$$
C =
0.15F_{\mathrm{slope}}
+ 0.45F_{\mathrm{stream}}
+ 0.40F_{\mathrm{HAND}}
$$

::: {.r-stack style="height: 500px; margin-top: -25px;"}

## 5. Take-home messages

:::{.fragment .fade-in}
- **Heavy rainfall does not produce the same pollution response everywhere.**
:::

:::{.fragment .fade-in}
- **The PPSI consistently identifies priority catchments for monitoring after heavy rainfall. Event-based field measurements remain necessary to confirm actual pollution.**
:::
